messages:
incident-bot: :warning: ALERT: Elevated throttle_events and sustained tokens/sec imbalance on inference-cluster-us-west-2. Autoscale throttle_count aggregate > 400 in 5m, paging eng-sre oncall.

noah: oncall here. Seeing sudden tokens/sec surge ~4x on model gptx-4a-std for a subset of customer routes. Dashboard shows queue depth per worker rising.

sylvia: quick note  we deployed routing tweak last night that prioritized gptx-4a-std for short-form completions. Could be routing amplification.

dan: jumping in. Are we seeing pod restarts or OOMs? Also curious if this is single AZ.

noah: no restarts. Metrics show higher token processing time and increased KV cache misses. Region scope: us-west-2 only so far.

ops-bot: autoscaler action queued (scale-request id=2036000001). Suggested target replicas +35%. Estimated node provisioning ~70s.

sylvia: mitigation proposal: 1) expand HPA headroom 2) enable fallback to gptx-4a-small for affected routes 3) suppress noisy per-pod throttle alerts while scale completes.

dan: +1. Also add a short lived route-rate-limit for the top offending customer keys to reduce hot-shard load. Support can message them.

noah: applying HPA bump: ```kubectl patch hpa inference-hpa -p '{"spec": {"maxReplicas": 160}}'``` watching.

ops-bot: scaling started, new worker nodes registering.

noah: enabling fallback via config service: ```PATCH /v1/routing/overrides {"fallback_model":"gptx-4a-small","scope":"routes:short_form","mode":"immediate"}``` response 200. Shift observed.

incident-bot: TAGS: customer_impact=degraded_throughput, impact_notes=brief stalls on a subset of streaming sessions (10-20s), a minority experienced token truncation. No total failures.

support-bot: Support heads-up: sending templated note to the top 6 customers by token volume in us-west-2.

sylvia: creating a temp grafana panel: "tokens/sec by model (top-k), qdepth 95th, aggregate_throttles" and shared link: https://grafana.internal/d/ai/auto-scale-hotspots (internal).

noah: telemetry improving; queue depth back down from ~400 to ~60 per pod, throttle_events trending down. Good.

dan: for follow-up: current alerts are too chatty. Per-pod queue-depth > 150 for 30s has been firing pages during normal spin-ups. Suggestions: bump to >220 for 3m, move to aggregate-style alert for throttles (sum across pods), and add a cooldown suppression when an autoscale event is in progress (e.g., suppress pages for 2m after scale start).

sylvia: also propose a tokens/sec anomaly rule per model: detect sustained deviation from baseline using moving median (example rule: WHEN rate(tokens_processed{model= "$MODEL"}[3m]) > 3x baseline_for_model FOR 2m THEN alert as "model_token_anomaly"). This helps catch model-specific hotspots.

dan: and add a pre-scale check in the alert pipeline: if HPA is already at or near maxReplicas, page immediately; else suppress until autoscale completes.

noah: logged mitigation steps here: HPA maxReplicas -> 160, fallback enabled to gptx-4a-small for short routes, temporary per-pod throttle alerts muted for 12m, support notified.

ops-bot: alert mute expired for per-pod throttles.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated (service_degraded). Pager cleared.

noah: next actions (owners):
- sylvia: create alert PR with concrete thresholds (queue-depth change, aggregate throttle alert, autoscale suppression logic).
- dan: add route-level rate-limits and customer throttles for heavy keys; coordinate support messages.
- noah: instrument scaled nodes with a scale_tag (scale_ticket=2036000001) and add short-lived metric to evaluate impact.

sylvia: drafting PR now. Draft alert expression: ```ALERT autoscale_saturation WHEN sum_over_time(throttle_events[3m]) > 120 AND avg_over_time(pod_queue_depth[3m]) > 220 FOR 3m```. Also adding label for autoscale_in_progress to suppress pages when true.

dan: logging request to sampling team: capture tokens/sec per model for 30m pre/post scaling for correlation.

incident-bot: note: added incident note pointing to routing change deploy yesterday as potential root cause.

sylvia: will also add a dashboard panel that shows deploys + routing weight changes over time for easier triage next time.

support-bot: tickets: 3 inbound so far, all acknowledged with templated note. No escalations.

noah: closing thread. Postmortem owners: noah (lead), sylvia (alerts/dashboard), dan (routing/rate-limits). Will open postmortem doc in docs-incidents repo. :white_check_mark:
